title: rel00.0-uc002 format: Implement size formatting, ANSI colors, and column alignment
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/format/ component -- responsibility and capabilities)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel00.0-uc002-format.yaml (use case for output formatting library)
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/ (find and read the PRD for pkg/format -- glob for prd*format*.yaml in this directory)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel-00.0.yaml (test suite for release 00.0, format section)
  - pkg/testutils/difftest.go (reference for existing package conventions: copyright header, SPDX, doc comments, naming)

files:
  - path: pkg/format/size.go
    action: create
    note: "Human-readable size formatting (bytes to K/M/G/T/P/E, binary and decimal bases)"
  - path: pkg/format/color.go
    action: create
    note: "ANSI color codes for Unix file types and permission display"
  - path: pkg/format/columns.go
    action: create
    note: "Column alignment for tabular output (ls -l style), width as parameter"

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement human-readable size formatting that converts byte counts to abbreviated suffixes (K, M, G, T, P, E). Support both binary base (powers of 1024, matching GNU --human-readable) and decimal base (powers of 1000, matching GNU --si). Format output to match GNU coreutils conventions: no space between number and suffix, one decimal digit when the value is less than 10."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement ANSI color output for Unix file types. Provide color codes for at least: directory (blue), symlink (cyan), executable (green), pipe/FIFO, socket, block device, character device, and regular file. Follow GNU LS_COLORS environment variable conventions for color assignment."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement column alignment for tabular output. Provide a type or function that formats rows into aligned columns with configurable padding, supporting both left-aligned and right-aligned columns. Accept output width as a parameter -- do not query terminal size. This supports ls -l, ls -C, and similar columnar layouts."
  - id: R4
    text: "Handle edge cases for all formatters: zero-byte sizes display as '0', size formatting handles values up to exabyte range without overflow, color output supports a no-color mode that emits no ANSI escape sequences, and column alignment handles empty input and single-column input without error."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "pkg/format does not import pkg/sys. Column alignment accepts width as a parameter; the caller obtains terminal width from pkg/sys or other sources."
  - id: D2
    text: "Follow existing package conventions from pkg/testutils/difftest.go: copyright header (Copyright (c) 2026 Petar Djukic. All rights reserved.), SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT, package doc comment referencing PRD requirement IDs with the Implements comment pattern."
  - id: D3
    text: "Use only the Go standard library (fmt, strconv, strings, os). Do not import golang.org/x/sys or any external dependency."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "go build ./pkg/format/ succeeds with no errors."
  - id: AC2
    text: "go vet ./pkg/format/ reports no issues."
  - id: AC3
    text: "pkg/format/size.go exports at least one function for human-readable size formatting that supports both binary (1024) and decimal (1000) base conversions."
  - id: AC4
    text: "pkg/format/color.go exports types or constants covering all seven Unix file types listed in R2, plus a mechanism to disable color output."
  - id: AC5
    text: "pkg/format/columns.go exports a type or function that aligns multi-column output given row data and a target width parameter."
  - id: AC6
    text: "All three source files include copyright header and package doc comment following the pattern in pkg/testutils/difftest.go."

title: rel00.0-uc002 format: Unit tests for prd003-format R1 (columns), R2 (color), R3 (size)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd003-format.yaml (requirements R1, R2, R3 and acceptance criteria)
  - pkg/format/size.go (HumanSize, HumanSizeOpts, formatValue implementation)
  - pkg/format/columns.go (Columns, PadRight, PadLeft, displayWidth implementation)
  - pkg/format/color.go (FileTypeColor, Reset, ColorEnabled, SetColorEnabled, ResetColorEnabled implementation)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel-00.0.yaml (test specifications for format use case)

files:
  - path: pkg/format/size_test.go
    action: create
    note: Table-driven unit tests for HumanSize in binary and SI modes
  - path: pkg/format/columns_test.go
    action: create
    note: Table-driven unit tests for Columns, PadRight, PadLeft
  - path: pkg/format/color_test.go
    action: create
    note: Unit tests for FileTypeColor, Reset, SetColorEnabled, ResetColorEnabled, ColorEnabled

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Test HumanSize with both binary mode (base 1024, suffixes K/M/G/T/P/E) and SI mode (base 1000, suffixes kB/MB/GB/TB): zero bytes returns \"0\", values under the base return the raw integer, boundary values at each unit threshold, one decimal place for values under 10 at a given unit, integer display for values 10 and above at a given unit (prd003-format R3.1, R3.2, R3.3, R3.4)"
  - id: R2
    text: "Test Columns layout with column-major ordering matching GNU ls, PadRight and PadLeft padding to specified display width, and displayWidth rune counting for multi-byte UTF-8 strings. Verify fallback to single-column when entries exceed terminal width, and nil return for empty input (prd003-format R1.1, R1.2, R1.3, R1.4)"
  - id: R3
    text: "Test FileTypeColor returns correct ANSI escape sequences for each file type -- directory (blue), symlink (cyan), executable (green), block device (yellow bold), char device (yellow bold), socket (magenta), pipe (yellow), and regular file (empty string). Test Reset returns the ANSI reset sequence (prd003-format R2.1, R2.2, R2.4)"
  - id: R4
    text: "Test SetColorEnabled(false) suppresses ANSI output from FileTypeColor and Reset (both return empty string), SetColorEnabled(true) forces ANSI output regardless of writer type, and ResetColorEnabled reverts to automatic TTY detection where ColorEnabled returns false for non-TTY writers like bytes.Buffer (prd003-format R2.3, R2.5, R2.6, R2.7)"

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Use table-driven tests with named subtests (t.Run) following Go testing conventions. Each test function uses a []struct with name, input fields, and expected output"
  - id: D2
    text: "Test color override by calling SetColorEnabled then verifying FileTypeColor and Reset output, followed by ResetColorEnabled in a t.Cleanup to restore automatic detection and avoid test pollution"
  - id: D3
    text: "Test ColorEnabled with a bytes.Buffer (non-TTY writer) to verify it returns false. TTY-positive testing is not feasible in automated test environments so only the negative path is tested directly"

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "go test ./pkg/format/... passes with zero failures"
  - id: AC2
    text: "HumanSize tests cover zero, sub-unit values, exact boundary values at K/M/G thresholds, values requiring one decimal place (e.g. 1536 bytes producing 1.5K), and both binary (opts.Binary true) and SI (opts.Binary false) modes"
  - id: AC3
    text: "Columns tests verify column-major layout for a known entry set at multiple terminal widths, single-column fallback when entries are wider than terminal width, nil return for empty input, and PadRight/PadLeft with ASCII and multi-byte UTF-8 strings"
  - id: AC4
    text: "FileTypeColor tests verify ANSI codes for all seven file types in color.go (directory, symlink, executable, block device, char device, socket, pipe) plus regular file returning empty string"
  - id: AC5
    text: "SetColorEnabled(false) causes FileTypeColor to return empty string for all file types and Reset to return empty string. SetColorEnabled(true) causes FileTypeColor to return ANSI codes and Reset to return the reset sequence. ResetColorEnabled restores automatic detection"

title: rel00.0-uc004 testutils: Implement DiffTest struct and differential test runner
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/testutils component description, data structures section for DiffTest, design decision DD2)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel00.0-uc004-testutils.yaml (testutils use case -- how the harness is invoked)
  - docs/specs/test-suites/test-rel-00.0.yaml (test suite for rel00.0 including testutils acceptance tests)
  - "docs/specs/product-requirements/ (find and read the testutils PRD in this directory -- filename matches prd*testutils*.yaml)"
  - go.mod (module path for package declaration)

files:
  - path: pkg/testutils/difftest.go
    action: create
    note: DiffTest struct, RunDiffTests function, comparison logic, normalization hooks

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Define an exported DiffTest struct with fields for: test name, command-line arguments, stdin input, environment variables, and expected exit code. The struct captures everything needed to run one differential test case against two binaries."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement an exported RunDiffTests function that accepts *testing.T, a path to the Go binary under test, a path to the reference GNU binary, and a slice of DiffTest cases. For each case, execute both binaries with identical stdin, arguments, and environment using os/exec, capturing stdout, stderr, and exit code from each."
  - id: R3
    text: "Compare stdout, stderr, and exit code from the Go binary against the reference binary for each test case. Report divergences via testing.T (t.Run per case, t.Errorf on mismatch), including the test name, input arguments, expected output from the reference binary, and actual output from the Go binary."
  - id: R4
    text: "Support normalization hooks -- optional caller-provided functions that transform stdout or stderr before comparison. Apply normalization to both reference and Go binary output before comparing. This handles known acceptable differences such as timestamps or temporary file paths."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Primary source file is difftest.go because the primary exported type is DiffTest. Project convention: name the file after the primary exported type, not the package name."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use os/exec.Command to invoke binaries. Pipe stdin from the test case via cmd.Stdin, capture stdout and stderr into bytes.Buffer, extract exit code via type assertion on *exec.ExitError from cmd.Run() error."
  - id: D3
    text: "Integrate with go test: RunDiffTests takes *testing.T and calls t.Run(tc.Name, ...) for each DiffTest case. Differential tests appear as standard Go subtests in test output and fail the test binary on any divergence."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "pkg/testutils/difftest.go exists and compiles without errors (go build ./pkg/testutils/...)."
  - id: AC2
    text: "DiffTest struct is exported with fields for Name, Args, Stdin, Env, and ExitCode at minimum."
  - id: AC3
    text: "RunDiffTests is exported and executes both the Go binary and reference binary per test case, comparing stdout, stderr, and exit code."
  - id: AC4
    text: "Normalization hooks are accepted by the API and applied to both outputs before comparison."
  - id: AC5
    text: "Code passes golangci-lint with no warnings (golangci-lint run ./pkg/testutils/...)."

title: rel00.0-uc003 sys: Implement prd002-sys R1 (terminal size), R2 (signal handling), R3 (file metadata)
description:
deliverable_type: code

required_reading:
  - docs/specs/product-requirements/prd002-sys.yaml (full PRD for pkg/sys -- requirements, design decisions, acceptance criteria)
  - docs/specs/use-cases/rel00.0-uc003-sys.yaml (use case for sys package)
  - docs/ARCHITECTURE.yaml (pkg/sys component description, design decision DD3, technology choices for golang.org/x/sys)
  - go.mod (module path and existing golang.org/x/sys dependency)
  - pkg/format/size.go (reference for file header, copyright, package doc comment, and code style conventions)
  - pkg/format/color.go (reference for existing isTerminal pattern -- pkg/sys provides terminal SIZE, not TTY detection)

files:
  - path: pkg/sys/terminal.go
    action: create
    note: Terminal size queries via TIOCGWINSZ ioctl using golang.org/x/sys/unix
  - path: pkg/sys/signal.go
    action: create
    note: Signal handling setup for SIGPIPE, SIGHUP, SIGWINCH
  - path: pkg/sys/stat.go
    action: create
    note: Common file metadata types and cross-platform accessor functions
  - path: pkg/sys/stat_darwin.go
    action: create
    note: Darwin-specific stat field access (Mtimespec, st_blocks as 512-byte units)
  - path: pkg/sys/stat_linux.go
    action: create
    note: Linux-specific stat field access (Mtim, st_blocks as 512-byte units)

requirements:
  - id: R1
    text: "Implement terminal size query function that returns terminal columns and rows via TIOCGWINSZ ioctl, per prd002-sys R1. Return a sensible default (80x24) when stdout is not a terminal. Use golang.org/x/sys/unix for the ioctl constant."
  - id: R2
    text: "Implement signal handling setup for SIGPIPE, SIGHUP, and SIGWINCH per prd002-sys R2. Provide functions to install handlers via Go os/signal package. SIGPIPE handler should set default behavior (exit silently). SIGWINCH handler should accept a callback for terminal resize notification."
  - id: R3
    text: "Implement file metadata abstraction that provides platform-independent access to modification time (time.Time) and disk block count (int64 in 512-byte units) from os.FileInfo, per prd002-sys R3. Use Go build tags to select Darwin (Mtimespec) or Linux (Mtim) stat field access."

design_decisions:
  - id: D1
    text: "Use golang.org/x/sys/unix for ioctl constants (TIOCGWINSZ) and platform-specific syscall_t field access. This is the only external dependency permitted by the architecture. cmd/ packages import pkg/sys, never golang.org/x/sys directly."
  - id: D2
    text: "Use Go build tags (//go:build darwin and //go:build linux) for platform-specific stat field access in separate files (stat_darwin.go, stat_linux.go). The common stat.go file defines exported types and functions that delegate to platform-specific helpers."
  - id: D3
    text: "Follow the file header and code style conventions established in pkg/format/: copyright header, SPDX license identifier, package doc comment referencing PRD requirement IDs, and Implements comments on exported functions."

acceptance_criteria:
  - id: AC1
    text: "pkg/sys/terminal.go exports a function that returns terminal columns and rows; returns 80x24 default when not a TTY"
  - id: AC2
    text: "pkg/sys/signal.go exports functions to install SIGPIPE, SIGHUP, and SIGWINCH handlers using os/signal"
  - id: AC3
    text: "pkg/sys/stat.go, stat_darwin.go, and stat_linux.go export functions that extract modification time and 512-byte block count from os.FileInfo on both platforms"
  - id: AC4
    text: "go build ./pkg/sys/... succeeds with no errors; go vet ./pkg/sys/... reports no issues"
